blocks.text: Selecting DOM Elements
Finding HTML Elements
Often, with JavaScript, you want to manipulate HTML elements.
To do so, you have to find the elements first. There are several ways to do this:

items: Finding HTML elements by tag name
Finding HTML elements by class name
Finding HTML elements by CSS selectors
Finding HTML elements by HTML object collections

blocks.text: Finding HTML Element by Id
The easiest way to find an HTML element in the DOM, is by using the element id.
This example finds the element with id="intro":
const element = document.getElementById("intro");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: If the element is found, the method will return the element as an object (in element).
If the element is not found, element will contain null.
Finding HTML Elements by Tag Name

This example finds all

elements:
const element = document.getElementsByTagName("p");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
This example finds the element with id="main", and then finds all

elements inside "main":

const x = document.getElementById("main");

const y = x.getElementsByTagName("p");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Finding HTML Elements by Class Name

If you want to find all HTML elements with the same class name, use
getElementsByClassName().
This example returns a list of all elements with class="intro".
const x = document.getElementsByClassName("intro");

blocks.text: Common Mistakes

items: Forgetting that querySelector() returns only the first match

blocks.text:
If you want to find all HTML elements that match a specified CSS selector
(id, class names, types, attributes, values of attributes, etc), use the querySelectorAll() method.

This example returns a list of all

elements with class="intro".
const x = document.querySelectorAll("p.intro");
